**Security: pass-with-notes** at `95bbd70a139feafedb16fbca2544383b410d636d`.

Whole phase-1 PR verdict: inventory code and revised workshop, using the complete `f5c25d4` assessment plus repair/merge deltas. Prior blocking shared-host, cached-ancestry and HEAD-coverage findings are closed as specified below. F88 enforcement is not yet deployed by this PR.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | ⚪ LOW | harness/scripts/route-inventory.json | 48 | Registration guard metadata describes native N, not the ordinary branch | 10/10 |
| 2 | ⚪ LOW | harness/scripts/route-inventory.json | 83 | POST background authority metadata omits parent | 10/10 |
| 3 | ⚪ LOW | harness/scripts/route-inventory.json | 335 | Compact-self send aliases omit parent-authorized controls | 10/10 |

These are nonblocking descriptive metadata notes, not executable authorization defects. Correct them before phase 2 consumes the inventory; operation-level checks remain authoritative.

## Blocking findings closed

The ruled owned-process/incarnation boundary, private issuer and ambiguity refusal prevent public session hints selecting another owned principal. This is design-contract closure, not implementation proof.

Every tokenless request now walks freshly to the nearest boundary, D16 bounded, with no cached ancestor authorization. The 4,096-entry boundary index is lookup metadata only and cannot bypass ancestry. Capacity exhaustion refuses registration rather than evicting boundaries. The H-M-S-P counterexample is retained as a phase-2 regression (`docs/plans/221-seat-provenance/workshops/001-capability-bootstrap.md:104-147`).

The probe includes HEAD and OPTIONS; all 12 implicit HEAD entries inherit GET classifications. HEAD `/v1/inbox` is inbox-claim, and background HEAD routes retain owner/parent protection (`crates/daemon/src/http/route_inventory_tests.rs:30-41,154-216`).

## Whole-PR classification and safety

The 77 unique pairs comprise 47 seat-authority, 29 machine-authenticated public and one independent job-token route. No false machine-public or HEAD/GET classification found. POST `/v1/steer` is attribution: the caller is resolved separately from the freely selectable target; audit/FYI are not caller authentication (`crates/daemon/src/http/steer.rs:122-235`).

Secure issuer first, owner-memory tokens, accepted-connection PID credentials, missing-evidence refusal, no bare-tuple TCP fallback and send-as-first enforcement order remain intact. Previously verified Tokio macOS PID support stands.

The test sensor has bounded per-call/overall timeouts and isolated fake-service/loopback fixtures; compilation/execution priority split and probe skip integration are present. No local execution or cost measurement was done; performance remains separately owned.

## Evidence and limits

Exact-head CI [42410293125](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42410293125), attempt 1, passed all four jobs. JUnit lists 2,169 passing cases, including real-router inventory and malformed/missing/stale/repeated/classification/job-token controls. HEAD-specific assertions were source-checked within these cases.

Phase 2 is not implemented; workstream s01 remains in-progress, not delivered. q-02 to q-04 remain permission-policy questions, not settled by authentication classification. Same-user private-state theft, connector delegation and execution within the owned process boundary remain stated residuals.

No C19/C21 disclosure found. No local tests/builds, sensor runs, probes, credentials, source edits or full imported-main implementation re-review. This is the current whole-PR verdict, superseding the old workshop-only disposition and unpublished `f5c25d4` source assessment.
